name: pimcore
_readme: Pimcore as migration target and as source. IMPORTANT SCOPE STATEMENT: Pimcore is primarily a PIM/MDM, DAM and CMS platform on Symfony; commerce comes from the OPTIONAL E-Commerce Framework bundle, which is a developer framework and not a finished shop. Treating Pimcore as a shop platform is the classic error in a fit estimation - the pack states this in the seed, in content_model_notes and in expected_hotspots_d3. Seed from general Pimcore/Symfony knowledge; every statement is a hypothesis until verified per engagement.

as_target.default_frontend: no shipped storefront - Twig templates rendered by the project's own Symfony controllers, or a fully self-built headless frontend over Data Hub

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered several Pimcore projects, is a certified Pimcore developer, knows the boundary between the PIM/DAM/CMS core and the optional E-Commerce Framework bundle precisely, and can say for any commerce requirement whether the framework provides a building block or only an interface to implement
snippets.docs_domains: pimcore.com/docs (Platform docs: Data Objects, Documents, Assets, Workflow Management, Data Hub, and the separate E-Commerce Framework section - always check which bundle a page belongs to), github.com/pimcore (pimcore/pimcore, ecommerce-framework-bundle, data-hub, data-importer, admin-ui-classic-bundle, studio-* - releases and UPGRADE.md are the reliable version and deprecation source), pimcore.com (editions, Pimcore Cloud, licensing), packagist.org for bundle maintenance status. A docs page existing does NOT mean the bundle is installed in the project - check composer.lock and config/bundles.php.
snippets.best_practice: model the domain in Data Object class definitions and EXPORT them to var/classes so the data model is in version control, never only in the database; extend by Symfony service decoration or aliasing in config/services.yaml and by event subscribers on DataObject/Asset/Document events, never by patching vendor/pimcore; override a bundle template by mirroring it under templates/bundles/<BundleName>/; use the E-Commerce Framework extension points as intended (own price system, availability system, checkout step, order agent, index tenant configured in the ecommerce-framework YAML) instead of bypassing the CartManager/OrderManager services; put anything bulk or slow behind Symfony Messenger or a Pimcore maintenance task, never in an admin request; choose the product index deliberately (default MySQL vs optimized MySQL vs Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) and size the reindex, because it decides the performance ceiling.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: which Pimcore major version and which bundles are actually installed, plus the deprecations of that line (admin-ui-classic vs Studio, removed legacy REST/Webservice API, bundle splits at 11.x - verify). D2: is the claimed standard counterpart core Pimcore, an official bundle, or an interface the project has to implement itself. D3: for every commerce requirement, does the E-Commerce Framework really ship it or only a contract for it - and is the requirement in fact a PIM/DAM/CMS requirement, where Pimcore is strong. D4: Data Hub GraphQL schema names are GENERATED per configuration and per class, so no endpoint name can be asserted without the project's Data Hub configuration; the same holds for the Simple REST adapter.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: FIRST separate the requirement into data/content vs shop: PIM/MDM (flexible attributes, localisation, relations, data quality, versioning), DAM, editorial CMS, workflows and multi-channel publishing are Pimcore's strengths and usually covered standard. Everything below is where a 'standard' claim must be challenged, because the E-Commerce Framework provides building blocks rather than finished features: checkout flows and payment breadth (each PSP is a separate bundle of varying maintenance); order management, order status handling, returns/RMA; promotions beyond what the Pricing Manager rule/condition/action model expresses; tax determination for multi-country scenarios; customer accounts and self-service; search relevance and merchandising (Index Service plus Elasticsearch, all relevance work is project work); B2B in full (organisation hierarchies, budgets, approvals, quotes, contract pricing, punchout - B2B needs custom development); subscriptions; multi-warehouse availability; shipping/carrier logic; anything a client calls 'standard shop functionality' out of habit.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: check before committing: there is NO shipped storefront and no shipped checkout UI, so the frontend and checkout are project scope in every case; the E-Commerce Framework is a framework - CartManager, CheckoutManager, PricingManager, OrderManager, IndexService are services to wire, and the checkout steps and payment providers are implemented per project (verify which payment provider bundles are maintained for the version in scope); Data Hub GraphQL operation names are generated from the class names and the Data Hub configuration, so an integration contract cannot be written before that configuration exists; the Simple REST adapter is read-only and Elasticsearch-backed (verify); Documents and their editables/bricks are Twig-rendered with no headless render contract, so a headless frontend must re-implement every brick; large object trees drive indexing and reindex cost and the MySQL default index is the usual performance wall; the Workflow Management engine is Symfony-Workflow-based configuration plus custom actions - real effort, not a switch; the admin UI line (classic ExtJS bundle vs the newer Studio UI) affects every admin extension the project has (verify per version); asset storage assumptions (local var/assets vs Flysystem S3) and the thumbnail pipeline break naive cloud moves.
snippets.content_model_notes: Three distinct content mechanisms, and the estimation must not blur them. (1) DOCUMENTS are the CMS: page, snippet, link, hardlink, email, newsletter, folder. Their editable content is a set of EDITABLES placed in a Twig template (input, wysiwyg, image, video, link, table, block, areablock, relation, ...). A page's structure is therefore fixed by the developer's template; only the editable values are business-editable. (2) BRICKS (area bricks) are the reusable component type: a PHP class implementing AreabrickInterface plus a Twig view, placed by editors inside an areablock - this is Pimcore's equivalent of a CMS component, and every brick is custom-built. (3) DATA OBJECTS with localised fields, field collections, object bricks and classification store are the PIM content - the strong part - and they carry product and entity content, not page layout. What renders out of the box: nothing editorial. Pimcore ships the mechanisms and the admin UI, not a set of ready components or a storefront. A headless target must map every brick and editable to a frontend component itself, since Documents render server-side Twig.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - names are GENERATED per Data Object class and per Data Hub configuration, so the project's Data Hub configuration is the only authoritative source

as_source.language_stack: PHP 8.x on Symfony 6/7, Doctrine, MySQL/MariaDB, Twig; Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and Redis optional but common
as_source.default_frontend: project-specific Twig templates rendered by own Symfony controllers, or a self-built headless frontend over Data Hub
do_not_run: bin/console pimcore:* (deployment:classes-rebuild, maintenance, cache:warmup, bundle:install, index rebuild)
bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate and any Pimcore migration command
any Elasticsearch/OpenSearch reindex or Data Importer run

snippets.version_markers: composer.json / composer.lock: pimcore/pimcore constraint is the AUTHORITATIVE major line; cross-check vendor/pimcore/pimcore/lib/Version.php (or Pimcore\Version::getVersion()). The bundle split matters as much as the version: presence of pimcore/admin-ui-classic-bundle, pimcore/ecommerce-framework-bundle, pimcore/data-hub, pimcore/data-importer, pimcore/customer-management-framework-bundle, pimcore/perspective-editor, pimcore/web-to-print-bundle in composer.lock tells you what the installation actually IS. Whether the E-Commerce Framework bundle is present at all decides whether this is a shop or a PIM. PHP version from composer.json require.php; Symfony line from symfony/framework-bundle. config/bundles.php (or src/Kernel.php in older lines) shows what boots.
snippets.active_units_config: AUTHORITATIVE = config/bundles.php - a bundle in vendor/ or src/ that is not registered there does not boot. Per-environment enablement additionally comes from config/packages/<env>/*.yaml. In older Pimcore lines bundles could be enabled at RUNTIME through the Extension Manager, whose state lived in var/config/extensions.php (or the database) - if the repository has such a file, read it; if the line predates config/bundles.php and no extensions state is in the repository, the enabled-bundle list must be requested from the client and nothing may be called dead until it arrives. Feature-level activation for commerce lives in the ecommerce-framework configuration (tenants, index, price systems), not in bundles.php.
snippets.package_sources: root composer.json require: pimcore/* official bundles, third-party bundles (payment providers, connectors), and project bundles required as path or VCS repositories; composer.lock for pinned versions and for spotting abandoned packages. Project code is src/ with the App\ namespace; separate project bundles may sit under bundles/ or src/<Name>Bundle. A bundle directory with no composer.lock entry is vendored by hand - flag it, it will not receive upstream fixes.
snippets.override_mechanisms: overridden = a Pimcore service replaced through Symfony DI in config/services.yaml: an alias from a Pimcore interface or service id to a project class, or a decorates: entry. This is the sanctioned mechanism - the interesting question per finding is which Pimcore contract was replaced and how far the replacement drifts from it. extended = a project class that subclasses a Pimcore class and is registered as an ADDITIONAL service without taking over the alias; also Data Object classes extended through the class definition's parentClass / useTraits / implementsInterfaces settings, which inject project code into GENERATED model classes. shadowed = a Twig template placed under templates/bundles/<BundleName>/<path> to shadow a bundle template (silent, path-based, no error if the upstream path moves), and public/ asset overrides. hooked = event subscribers on Pimcore events (DataObjectEvents, AssetEvents, DocumentEvents, AdminEvents, and the E-Commerce Framework's own events) - additive, several subscribers on one event run by priority, so behaviour depends on priority values. configured = the E-Commerce Framework extension points (own price system, availability system, checkout step, checkout manager, order agent, index tenant, filter type) selected in the ecommerce-framework YAML: these are intended replacements, not overrides, and should be classified as standard-extension work rather than customisation depth.
snippets.schema_sources: var/classes/definition_<Class>.php - Data Object CLASS DEFINITIONS: fields, localized fields, field collections, object bricks, classification store, and the parentClass/interfaces hooks. var/classes/DataObject/*.php are GENERATED from them (do not count them as custom code). var/classes/fieldcollections/, var/classes/objectbricks/, var/classes/customlayouts/ likewise. CRITICAL TRAP: class definitions are stored in the DATABASE and only mirrored into var/classes when the project exports them - a repository without definition_* files means the data model is invisible to a code-only analysis and must be requested as an export; say so instead of reporting a small data model. Relational schema beyond that: Doctrine migrations under src/Migrations or <bundle>/Migrations, config/packages/pimcore*/*.yaml, and Elasticsearch index mappings inside the ecommerce-framework configuration.
snippets.workflow_sources: Pimcore Workflow Management configured in YAML (config/packages/*.yaml, pimcore.workflows): places, transitions, guards, notification and custom actions on Data Objects, Documents and Assets - Symfony Workflow underneath. Plus: E-Commerce Framework checkout manager steps and the order agent's order state handling; Symfony Messenger handlers and their transport configuration; Pimcore maintenance tasks (Pimcore\Maintenance\TaskInterface) and the 5-minute pimcore:maintenance cron; Data Importer configurations for recurring data flows. The crontab and the Messenger worker supervision are infrastructure, not repository - request them.
snippets.data_script_sources: Doctrine migration up()/down(); bundle Installer classes (install/uninstall SQL, class definition import, permission setup); src/Command/* console commands; Pimcore Data Importer configurations (definition per import, usually in var/config or config/); Data Hub configurations; thumbnail and video-thumbnail configurations; classification store definitions; direct Pimcore\Db SQL in services (flag it - it bypasses model events, versioning and cache invalidation, exactly the behaviour a migration to another platform loses silently).
snippets.read_order: composer.json + composer.lock (which bundles exist at all - especially whether ecommerce-framework-bundle is present), config/bundles.php (what boots), config/packages/** (pimcore*, pimcore_ecommerce_framework, workflows, security, messenger, flysystem), var/classes/definition_* (the data model, if exported), then src/: Controller/, Document/Areabrick/, EventListener/ or EventSubscriber/, Model/, Service/, Command/, Migrations/, then templates/ (areas/<brick>, documents, includes, bundles/<Bundle> overrides), then public/. Finally vendor/pimcore for the contract actually being decorated or subclassed. Do not assert an effective configuration value from a bundle default - Symfony merges config/packages by environment, and the project value wins.
snippets.hosting_constraints: self-hosted (usually Docker: php-fpm, MySQL/MariaDB, Redis, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Supervisor) or Pimcore Cloud - the hosting model must be established before any operational claim. Assets go through Flysystem: a project assuming the local var/assets adapter needs rework for object storage, and the on-demand thumbnail pipeline writes into public/var/tmp/thumbnails, which needs a writable and shared volume or a CDN in front. Elasticsearch/OpenSearch is required for the optimized product index and for the Simple REST adapter (verify). Redis for cache and sessions in any multi-node setup. Symfony Messenger workers must be supervised, and the pimcore:maintenance cron must run every few minutes - both are infrastructure the repository cannot prove. The classic admin UI is memory- and time-hungry on large object trees, so PHP memory_limit, max_execution_time and upload limits are functional constraints, not just ops details.
